prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / ui-mockup.
Asset type: one polished portrait mobile-game level screen visual concept, 1080×1920, no phone bezel, no presentation board.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the actual game screenshot 540×960. Input image 2 is a SUPPORTING reference of the EXISTING background only. The user wants a new lower-screen presentation of little dragons puffing their cheeks and blowing colored bubbles upward.

IMMUTABLE AREA: Preserve the entire screenshot from the top through the glowing horizontal cyan warning line at y≈560/960 (58.5% of height), inclusive. Keep top pause button, 第7关 label, progress bar and 0%, cloud strip, the dense tiny colored-bubble mosaic with its exact same picture, all colors/positions/scaling/layout, and the warning line. Treat this upper region as a locked pasted photographic screenshot, not something to reinterpret or redraw. Keep the original background throughout the whole screen: the same blue sky above and pale blue misty cloud-bordered backdrop below. Do NOT replace the scenery or create new architecture, water, terrain, forests, or gardens.

CHANGE ONLY FOREGROUND BELOW THE WARNING LINE, roughly lower 41% of image.
Design direction: a charming little bubble-dragon squad, clearly readable, premium rounded toy-like 2.5D casual game art, soft bright lighting, glassy colorful bubbles, matching the existing cheerful blue game. The dragons are appealing original small friendly dragons, plump bodies, short rounded snouts, two tiny rounded horns, cream bellies, little dorsal bumps, small curled tails, big lively eyes. They are fully dimensional characters with heads and bodies, not round face-only icons. No scary dragons, flames, guns, cannons or machines.

Composition for the lower foreground:
1) Immediately under the warning line is an OPEN dragon firing row spanning the width, around y=590–690/960. This row is the main visual focal point. Place three visibly active dragons at separated positions (a bright green dragon, a sky-blue dragon, and a coral-pink dragon), with the green dragon slightly more prominent. Show them in a readable three-quarter/profile view with snouts tilted UP toward the bubble board, rounded cheeks clearly puffed out, focused joyful eyes, and a small O-shaped mouth. Show an unambiguous chain of TWO OR THREE colored glossy bubbles coming directly out of each dragon's mouth and rising toward the warning line. Green dragon blows green bubbles, blue dragon blue bubbles, pink dragon pink bubbles. These are thin pearlescent colored soap bubbles, not solid candies. Trails remain below the warning line so the existing board is untouched. A half-formed bubble attached to one dragon's lips makes the action absolutely clear. The dragon heads, cheeks and upward breath must be the most appealing and legible detail.
Keep a row of eight small understated placement spots across this zone: six available positions including the three occupied ones, with two smaller pale locked positions at the far right. Replace the heavy existing glowing mechanical dishes with light little translucent oval foot markers; avoid a big panel surrounding this row. Active dragons may overlap their own foot markers naturally.
2) Beneath the firing row, around y=725–870/960, redesign the queue into FIVE tidy side-by-side OPEN waiting lanes, each containing THREE smaller baby dragons with varied colors (green, blue, coral red, peach, purple) in depth order. No glass cylinders, no tubes, no cages, no bottles, no large rectangular lane frames. Use tiny soft shadows and subtle curved pale-blue floor markings to imply orderly queues. Their cute faces, tiny horns and curled tails create a family identity with the firing dragons. Head of each queue is visually clear and slightly larger. Preserve small legible white numeric counters on compact blue lozenges attached near each character, as in the current gameplay, without clutter.
3) At the bottom around y=905–950/960, make three concise rounded glossy action buttons, slimmer and calmer than the original huge heavy frames, with a white shuffle icon and exact Chinese text “重排”, a double-chevron icon and exact text “优先出战”, and a small multicolored bubble icon and exact text “泡泡炸弹”. Blue, warm gold and violet button accents respectively. Small use-count badges “2”, “2”, “1”. No additional text, titles, decorative logos, explanations or captions.

The result should look like a believable production game screen after replacing ONLY its lower foreground art, not a poster. Priority order: locked original upper board and warning line; unchanged existing background; clearly puffed cheeks and upward mouth-origin bubbles; coherent dragon squad; spacious playable lower UI. Keep the lower area airy, emphasize characters, avoid piles of decorative stars/clouds that hide the background. No new rules or aiming line. Deliver one full-screen portrait.
